messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: PROD kv-allocator anomaly in us-east-1. Elevated CUDA malloc failures and kv cache fragmentation detected. Error rate 4.2x baseline, 99th latency spike, a few requests returning 5xx. Paging oncall-ml. thread_ts=2076543210
alice: oncall-ml here, picking this up. I see the alert. Can someone dump the top hosts by OOM count? :raised_hand:
bob: grabbing logs, running quick query against metrics. top hosts: gpu-04, gpu-07, gpu-12. Continuous-batching queues show runaway batch sizes on those hosts.
carla: seeing a lot of arena fragmentation in logs, repeated cudaMalloc retries then fallback to CPU path. stack traces point to kv_arena.py::alloc_slot and PyTorch malloc churn.
dinesh: this smells like the recent batch sizing heuristic regress we rolled yesterday (optimizer for throughput). Could be enabling larger async batches causing fragmentation. Suggest immediate mitigation: throttle continuous batching config to disable async batching on affected pool.
alice: agree. Can we hotflip the batch config for the pool to conservative? How fast is config propagation?
eva: config push will hit service mesh; should be <30s for agents to pick up. I'll patch a conservative override targeting pool=kv_pool_us_east1 with batch.max_inflight=4 and batch.async=false.
carla: before patching, let's snapshot the KV cache stats to baseline for later analysis. run: `redwood-admin kv-stats --pool kv_pool_us_east1 --hosts gpu-04,gpu-07,gpu-12 --output json > /tmp/kvstats_2076543210.json`
bob: starting snapshot now.
alice: also, run arena compaction on affected hosts as a remediation step. Command we use:```shell
redwood-admin arena-compact --pool kv_pool_us_east1 --hosts gpu-04,gpu-07,gpu-12 --mode aggressive
```This will free fragmented arenas; may spike latency briefly. call it out to CS.
dinesh: I'll prepare a short customer impact blurb. preliminary: some requests experienced transient 5xx and tail latency > 2x for embeddings/generation on affected hosts between 12:07-12:35 UTC. No data leak or model drift.
cs-notify-bot: Drafting customer notifications for accounts with high traffic routed through us-east-1. ETA 8m.
alice: deploy the batch config override now. eva please push and verify agents pick up.
eva: pushing override: ```yaml
pool: kv_pool_us_east1
overrides:
  batch:
    max_inflight: 4
    async: false
```Pushed at 12:09 UTC. agents reported SUCCESS on gpu-04,gpu-07,gpu-12.
deploy-bot: config-override/kv-batch-2076543210 deployed to 3 hosts (gpu-04,gpu-07,gpu-12) at 12:09:22 UTC. rollout=canary(3/200).
bob: metrics after override: batch sizes collapsed to target, cuda malloc failure rate down ~60% on those hosts. still seeing fragmentation backlog though.
dinesh: start arena compaction now on the three hosts. Expect brief latency bump for compaction duration (~30s per host).
action: carla ran compaction at 12:12 UTC. logs show success, freed ~1.8GB across hosts.
alice: monitoring latency and 5xx for whole pool. early signals look good: 99th latency creeping down, error rate trending back to baseline.
carla: there are a couple of hosts with persistent slab leak indicators (delta in retained pages not recovered by compaction). We'll isolate those and drain traffic.
eva: marking gpu-07 as drain: `redwood-admin host-drain gpu-07 --reason "allocator-degeneracy"` routed traffic away within 40s.
sre-rotation: initiating node-recycle for gpu-07; will reboot and run full memory sanitizer on restart.
alice: oncall-ml to continue observing for 30m, then hand over. who is next for handoff?
oncall-ml: I'm staying for first 30m. After that, @sre-rotation will take primary. leaving a short checklist: 1) ensure batch override stays enforced, 2) monitor kv-stats for retained pages, 3) coordinate node-recycle progress.
dinesh: customer-impact list: identified 9 mid/large customers with >5% requests routed through affected hosts. CS is preparing targeted comms. Severity: S2 (user-facing latency and transient errors, mitigation in effect).
cs-notify-bot: sent targeted notifications to affected accounts at 12:18 UTC. content included workaround (route to other regions via region pinning) and ETA for full fix.
bob: started a deeper heap/profile capture on gpu-12 to understand fragmentation root cause. saving capture to s3://redwood-dumps/kv-frag/2076543210/heap_gpu-12.pbz2
carla: interesting note: PyTorch's caching allocator stats show many small free blocks never coalesced due to allocation pattern with large async batches. That plus a recent change in our allocator arena threshold likely increased fragmentation.
alice: agreed. Next steps for postmortem: 1) revert batch heuristic change globally until we have better compaction heuristics, 2) add tighter canary gating for batch size changes, 3) add automatic arena compaction fallback when fragmentation metric crosses X, 4) improve observability on per-host retained pages.
dinesh: I'll open the incident in Jira and assign owners for the above items. Incident ticket: REDWOOD-INT-207654.
oncall-ml: handing over to @sre-rotation at 12:39 UTC. leaving monitoring to them.
sre-rotation: thanks — taking over. Summary received. continuing to watch, will coordinate the node-recycle and follow up with a short incident report in #postmortems.
deploy-bot: patch revert/batch-heuristic-2076543210 scheduled to canary at 13:10 UTC (manual approval required).
alice: tagging follow-ups: @dinesh (postmortem lead), @carla (alloc debug), @eva (observability), @bob (telemetry export). Please add timeline and link heap dump.
carla: added initial debug notes to the incident ticket and uploaded artifacts.
sre-rotation: marking thread as ongoing but mitigated. will update on final status and RCA. :thumbsup: :grimacing:
